newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA SELECTS THREE BIDS FOR OTELINOX.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA SELECTS THREE BIDS FOR OTELINOX.

text.p: Samsung Deutschland GmbH and Italy's Stainless Steel International SpA and Finven SpA will start talks with Romanian authorities next week on sale of 51 percent in a local steel maker, officials said.

"We accepted three of the four bids we had for Otelinox and we'll start negotiations seeking the best price," Sebastian Vladescu, state secretary in the Industry Ministry and chairman of the selection commission said on Tuesday.
"Investment commitments will also be considered," he added.
Vladescu, who was speaking to reporters after the opening of the sealed bids, said a fourth bid -- from Krupp Thyssen of Germany -- had been rejected.
"Krupp wanted to buy part of an asset," he said. "To be able to sell that we should have had to split Otelinox first."

The minimum selling price for the stake in Otelinox, Romania's sole stainless steel maker, was set at around $44 million, Vladescu said. The price was set by Otelinox's main stockholder, the State Ownership Fund (FPS).

Forthcoming talks on the selloff follow an aborted tender in June in which four bidders -- the three companies selected on Tuesday and France's Ugine, belonging to Usinor Sacilor -- failed to meet the minimum selling price.
"This time, the FPS will accept the best bid, even if it goes below the set price," Vladescu said. Details of the bids remained confidential.

Otelinox, which officials say is the most modern such plant in central and eastern Europe, is based in Tirgoviste, 83 km (51 miles) north-east of Bucharest. It has a share capital of 141 billion lei in shares with a face value of 25,000 lei each.
The company had a net profit of 7.5 billion lei last year, up from 4.5 billion lei in 1995, which had reversed a 1994 loss of 4.6 billion lei.
It recently joined the Bucharest bourse's first tier, after trading on the over-the-counter market. On Tuesday it closed 500 lei higher at 51,500.
